items.followUp: What is the resultant of two like parallel forces?

rubric.why: Identifies what makes parallel forces like.
rubric.description: States that like parallel forces act in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating their directions are the same.

rubric.why: Identifies the contrasting direction of unlike parallel forces.
rubric.description: States that unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating their directions are opposite.

modelAnswer: Like parallel forces act in the same direction.
Unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.

items.followUp: State the condition for rotational equilibrium of a body.

rubric.why: Identifies one side of the moments balance.
rubric.description: Mentions the sum of clockwise moments about the pivot or turning point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying clockwise moments.

rubric.why: Completes the moments balance required by the principle.
rubric.description: States that clockwise moments equal anticlockwise moments about the same pivot or turning point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the equality of the two moment sums.

modelAnswer: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of its clockwise moments about a pivot is equal to the sum of its anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.

items.followUp: A force of 8 N moves an object 3 m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done.

rubric.why: Includes the defining physical quantities for work.
rubric.description: Defines work as done when a force causes displacement in its direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating work to force and displacement in the direction of the force.
Award 1 mark for a correct formula, such as W = Fd.

modelAnswer: Work is done when a force causes displacement of an object in the direction of the force.

items.followUp: Write the formula for kinetic energy and state what each symbol represents.

rubric.why: Defines kinetic energy by the condition associated with it.
rubric.description: Defines kinetic energy as the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the energy of a body to its motion.

rubric.why: Gives the standard expression for kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula, KE = ½mv².

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.

items.followUp: How much work must be done in one second for a device to have a power of one watt?

rubric.why: Names the S.I. unit being defined.
rubric.description: Identifies the unit of power as the watt.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the watt.

rubric.why: States the work and time that define one watt.
rubric.description: Defines one watt as a rate of doing one joule of work in one second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both the one-joule work and one-second time.

modelAnswer: The S.I. unit of power is the watt (W).
A device has a power of one watt when it does one joule of work in one second.

items.followUp: A force of 20 N acts on an area of 4 m². Calculate the pressure.

rubric.why: States the defining force-to-area relationship for pressure.
rubric.description: Defines pressure as force acting per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or equivalent formula.

rubric.why: Identifies the S.I. unit of pressure.
rubric.description: Gives the S.I. unit as the pascal (Pa), equivalent to N/m².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for pascal or an equivalent unit.

modelAnswer: Pressure is the force acting per unit area.
Its S.I. unit is the pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

items.followUp: What happens to pressure applied to an enclosed liquid according to Pascal’s law?

rubric.why: Establishes that the law concerns pressure applied to an enclosed fluid.
rubric.description: States that pressure is applied to an enclosed fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the enclosed fluid and applied pressure.

rubric.why: Gives the key transmission property in Pascal’s law.
rubric.description: States that the applied pressure is transmitted undiminished throughout the fluid, in all directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pressure is transmitted undiminished or equally throughout the fluid.

modelAnswer: When pressure is applied to an enclosed fluid, it is transmitted undiminished to every part of the fluid and to the walls of its container.

items.followUp: What happens to the shape of an elastic body when the deforming force is removed?

rubric.why: Recognises elasticity as a property or ability of a body.
rubric.description: Identifies elasticity as a property or ability of a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing elasticity as a property or ability.

rubric.why: States the defining recovery after the deforming force is removed.
rubric.description: States that the body returns to its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing recovery of the original shape or size after removal of the force.

modelAnswer: Elasticity is the property of a body by which it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.
